slides.title: PINCH / TECTONIC
slides.subtitle: Bristol went back to the root.
slides.image_concept: Bristol floating harbour at night, industrial dockside silhouettes, fog, dark and still
slides.image_keywords: Bristol harbour night fog industrial docks

slides.text:
Bristol, 2004.
Rob Ellis drives to London.
FWD>>. Plastic People.
He watches Kode9 from the crowd.
He drives home and builds a label.
slides.image_concept: Night motorway from dashboard perspective, distant city lights ahead, dark interior
slides.image_keywords: night motorway dashboard view city lights

slides.text:
2005. Tectonic Recordings.
First release: 'War Dub.'
Not London. Not Croydon. Bristol.
A city with dub in its soil.
slides.image_concept: Vinyl record white label extreme close-up, only a catalogue number visible, minimal
slides.image_keywords: vinyl record white label close-up catalogue number

slides.text:
2006. 'Qawwali.'
He found a harmonium recording
by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan.
He slowed it. He buried it in bass.
It sounded like Bristol.
It sounded like Karachi.
It became dubstep's defining track.
slides.image_concept: Harmonium keyboard instrument close-up, dark room, faint light on the keys
slides.image_keywords: harmonium keyboard instrument close-up dark room

slides.text:
Tectonic housed the underground.
Loefah. Digital Mystikz. Skream.
Distance. Flying Lotus. Peverelist. Joker.
It was not a movement.
It was a room for the serious.
slides.image_concept: Record shop interior, 12-inch vinyl racks in near-darkness, a single hand pulling out a sleeve
slides.image_keywords: record shop 12 inch vinyl rack hand browsing dark

slides.text:
2007. Underwater Dancehall.
Dubstep's first real album.
Two discs. One instrumental. One vocal.
MC Juakali from New York
over Bristol bass.
No compromise.
slides.image_concept: Underwater looking upward to the surface, light rippling, deep blue tones
slides.image_keywords: underwater looking up surface light blue dark

slides.text:
2011. Pinch & Shackleton.
Two of the most serious minds
in bass music. One album.
Ritual percussion. Deep root bass.
Critics ran out of words.
slides.image_concept: Two dark lines crossing in abstract space, monochrome, minimal, fog-like
slides.image_keywords: two lines intersect abstract dark minimal monochrome

slides.text:
Twenty years of Tectonic.
The root was always there.
Someone just needed to stay close to it.

Save this.
slides.image_concept: Tree roots close-up, dark soil, strong texture, underground power
slides.image_keywords: tree roots dark soil underground close-up texture
